subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the broader TUI scroll-jump fix be owned as OpenClaw viewport/follow state, a pi-tui renderer dependency repair, or an explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: Source evidence shows the behavior is still plausible on current main, but the durable fix changes user-facing terminal scroll semantics and crosses a third-party renderer boundary.

options.title: OpenClaw TUI anchoring policy
options.body: Implement TUI-owned viewport anchoring/follow behavior and validate it with live PTY proof while coordinating dependency behavior with the narrower scrollback issue.

options.title: Renderer-first repair
options.body: Wait for or carry a pi-tui fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing scrollback, then verify whether this broader issue is fully resolved.

options.title: Add a preference
options.body: Expose a TUI auto-scroll/follow setting only if maintainers want configurable behavior instead of a fixed non-disruptive default.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw TUI anchoring policy
recommendation.body: Implement TUI-owned viewport anchoring/follow behavior and validate it with live PTY proof while coordinating dependency behavior with the narrower scrollback issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and pi-tui/TUI integration context make steipete the best available routing candidate for the product/dependency boundary decision.
